subject: rstan::extract does not include initial value

messages.author: 77e72e34bf8c033f
messages.subject: rstan::extract does not include initial value
parts:
Hi all

I have noticed that sometimes my traceplots, including warmup, do not start at the initial value I used. Here is an example:

> head(rstan::extract(sfit, pars = 'var1', inc_warmup = T, permuted = F))
[1] -0.01354534 -0.01354534 -0.01354534 -0.01354534 -0.01354534 -0.01354534
> xxx2 <- get_inits(sfit)
> xxx2[[1]]$var1
[1] 0
> 

Should I be worried about offsets in my parameter estimations?

Thanks for an awesome tool!

Best,
Per

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: rstan::extract does not include initial value
parts:
Hi Per, 

I'm not sure what you mean by "offsets in parameter estimations", but I don't think you should be worried. rstan::extract with inc_warmup=TRUE will return the draws for iteration 1 through the final iteration. You can prepend the initial values obtained from get_inits() manually if you want to, but either way the only draws you should use for inference are those that comprise the post-warmup posterior sample (the combined post-warmup draws from all chains). 

Hope that helps, but let me know if I've misunderstood your question. 

Jonah

messages.author: 77e72e34bf8c033f
messages.subject: Re: rstan::extract does not include initial value
parts:
Hi Jonah,

thank you for your reply.

What I meant with "offsets in parameter estimations", was if one expects rstan::extract to return the entire chain, including all warmup and post-warmup samples, with the very first sample having the value that you specified as the initial value, then if the very first sample does NOT have the specified initial value, it could imply that all samples had been shifted with this value: difference = specified initial value - actual initial value.

For my final inference I only use post-warmup samples :)

However, I almost always inspect the entire traceplot of both warmup and post-warmup samples, to see if I can improve my sampling efficiency by tweaking my priors, warmup lengths, initializations etc.

Best,
Per
